page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled. The instance is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-standard-8 in the lower performance tiers for compute-heavy tasks. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, along with Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, rank in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 10%. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks (both read and write) and Passmark memory scores perform at an average level, placing in the middle 50%. Ray tracing workloads also achieve average performance, while static web serving throughput and database operations remain in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio offer a predictable resource profile for standard workloads without the risk of CPU credit exhaustion. Given its performance profile, this instance is best suited for moderate general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, light software compilation, and small-scale text or image processing tasks that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
